p155.original: A monetary policy that lowers interest rates and stimulates borrowing is an expansionary monetary policy or loose monetary policy. Conversely, a monetary policy that raises interest rates and reduces borrowing in the economy is a contractionary monetary policy or tight monetary policy. This module will discuss how expansionary and contractionary monetary policies affect interest rates and aggregate demand, and how such policies will affect macroeconomic goals like unemployment and inflation. We will conclude with a look at the Fed’s monetary policy practice in recent decades.
p155.zh: 降低利率和刺激借贷的货币政策是一种扩张性的货币政策或宽松的货币政策. 相反,提高利率和减少经济借款的货币政策是收缩性的货币政策或紧缩的货币政策。 本单元将讨论扩张和收缩的货币政策如何影响利率和总需求,以及这些政策如何影响失业和通货膨胀等宏观经济目标。 最后,我们将审视美联储近几十年来的货币政策做法。

p156.original: The Effect of Monetary Policy on Interest Rates
p156.zh: 货币政策对利率的影响

p157.original: Consider the market for loanable bank funds in . The original equilibrium (E0) occurs at an 8% interest rate and a quantity of funds loaned and borrowed of $10 billion. An expansionary monetary policy will shift the supply of loanable funds to the right from the original supply curve (S0) to S1, leading to an equilibrium (E1) with a lower 6% interest rate and a quantity $14 billion in loaned funds. Conversely, a contractionary monetary policy will shift the supply of loanable funds to the left from the original supply curve (S0) to S2, leading to an equilibrium (E2) with a higher 10% interest rate and a quantity of $8 billion in loaned funds.
p157.zh: 考虑银行可贷款资金的市场。最初的平衡(E0)以8%的利率和100亿美元贷款和借款的数量发生.扩张性货币政策将把可贷款资金的供应从原来的供应曲线(S0)转向S1,从而实现利率6%以下的平衡(E1),贷款资金数量为140亿美元。 相反,收缩的货币政策将把可贷款资金的供应从原来的供应曲线(S0)转向S2,从而实现利率10%更高、贷款资金80亿美元的平衡(E2)。

p159.original: How does a central bank “raise” interest rates? When describing the central bank's monetary policy actions, it is common to hear that the central bank “raised interest rates” or “lowered interest rates.” We need to be clear about this: more precisely, through open market operations the central bank changes bank reserves in a way which affects the supply curve of loanable funds. As a result,  shows that interest rates change. If they do not meet the Fed’s target, the Fed can supply more or less reserves until interest rates do.
p159.zh: 中央银行如何“提高”利率? 在描述央行的货币政策行动时,人们通常会听到央行“提高利率”或“降低利率 ” 。 我们需要明确这一点:更确切地说,央行通过开放市场运作改变银行储备,从而影响可贷款资金的供应曲线。 因此,表明利率有变化。 如果它们达不到美联储的目标,美联储可以提供多少储备,直到利率达到.

p160.original: Recall that the specific interest rate the Fed targets is the federal funds rate. The Federal Reserve has, since 1995, established its target federal funds rate in advance of any open market operations.
p160.zh: 回顾美联储的具体利率目标是联邦基金利率。 自1995年以来,联邦储备局在开放市场运作之前就确定了其联邦基金目标利率。

p161.original: Of course, financial markets display a wide range of interest rates, representing borrowers with different risk premiums and loans that they must repay over different periods of time. In general, when the federal funds rate drops substantially, other interest rates drop, too, and when the federal funds rate rises, other interest rates rise. However, a fall or rise of one percentage point in the federal funds rate—which remember is for borrowing overnight—will typically have an effect of less than one percentage point on a 30-year loan to purchase a house or a three-year loan to purchase a car. Monetary policy can push the entire spectrum of interest rates higher or lower, but the forces of supply and demand in those specific markets for lending and borrowing set the specific interest rates.
p161.zh: 当然,金融市场显示出广泛的利率,代表着风险溢价不同的借款人和必须在不同时期偿还的贷款.一般来说,当联邦基金利率大幅下降时,其他利率也会下降,当联邦基金利率上升时,其他利率也会上升. 然而,联邦基金利率下降或上升一个百分点(记住是一晚上借的),通常会对购买房屋的30年贷款或购买汽车的3年贷款产生不到一个百分点的影响。货币政策可以推动整个利率的提高或降低,但这些特定借贷市场的供求力量规定了具体的利率。

p162.original: The Effect of Monetary Policy on Aggregate Demand
p162.zh: 货币政策对总需求的影响

p163.original: Monetary policy affects interest rates and the available quantity of loanable funds, which in turn affects several components of aggregate demand. Tight or contractionary monetary policy that leads to higher interest rates and a reduced quantity of loanable funds will reduce two components of aggregate demand. Business investment will decline because it is less attractive for firms to borrow money, and even firms that have money will notice that, with higher interest rates, it is relatively more attractive to put those funds in a financial investment than to make an investment in physical capital. In addition, higher interest rates will discourage consumer borrowing for big-ticket items like houses and cars. Conversely, loose or expansionary monetary policy that leads to lower interest rates and a higher quantity of loanable funds will tend to increase business investment and consumer borrowing for big-ticket items.
p163.zh: 货币政策影响利率和可贷款资金的现有数量,而这又影响总需求的若干组成部分。导致利率上升和可贷款资金数量减少的紧缩或紧缩货币政策将减少总需求的两个组成部分。企业投资将下降,因为借款对公司吸引力较小,即使有资金的公司也会注意到,利率较高,将这些资金投入金融投资比投入实物资本更具吸引力。 此外,较高的利率将阻止消费者为房屋和汽车等大用品借款。 相反,导致利率降低和可贷款资金数量增加的宽松或扩张的货币政策,往往会增加企业投资和消费者对大项目借贷。

p164.original: If the economy is suffering a recession and high unemployment, with output below potential GDP, expansionary monetary policy can help the economy return to potential GDP.  (a) illustrates this situation. This example uses a short-run upward-sloping Keynesian aggregate supply curve (SRAS). The original equilibrium during a recession of E0 occurs at an output level of 600. An expansionary monetary policy will reduce interest rates and stimulate investment and consumption spending, causing the original aggregate demand curve (AD0) to shift right to AD1, so that the new equilibrium (E1) occurs at the potential GDP level of 700.
p164.zh: 如果经济正遭受衰退和高失业率,产出低于潜在的国内生产总值,扩张性货币政策可以帮助经济恢复到潜在的国内生产总值。(a) 说明这种情况。 这个例子使用一个短跑的向上倾斜的凯恩斯式总供给曲线(SRAS).E0衰退期间的原始平衡发生在产出水平为600.扩张性货币政策将降低利率,刺激投资和消费支出,使最初的总需求曲线(AD0)向AD1转变,从而实现新的平衡(E1),其潜在GDP水平为700。

p165.zh: 扩张性或收缩性货币政策

p166.original: Conversely, if an economy is producing at a quantity of output above its potential GDP, a contractionary monetary policy can reduce the inflationary pressures for a rising price level. In  (b), the original equilibrium (E0) occurs at an output of 750, which is above potential GDP. A contractionary monetary policy will raise interest rates, discourage borrowing for investment and consumption spending, and cause the original demand curve (AD0) to shift left to AD1, so that the new equilibrium (E1) occurs at the potential GDP level of 700.
p166.zh: 相反,如果一个经济体的产出数量超过其潜在的国内总产值,则收缩性货币政策可以减少通货膨胀压力,使物价水平上升。 在(b)中,原始平衡(E0)发生在750个产出上,高于潜在的国内生产总值。收缩的货币政策将提高利率,抑制投资和消费支出的借贷,并导致原有的需求曲线(AD0)左转至AD1,从而实现新的平衡(E1),其潜在GDP水平为700。

p167.original: These examples suggest that monetary policy should be countercyclical; that is, it should act to counterbalance the business cycles of economic downturns and upswings. The Fed should loosen monetary policy when a recession has caused unemployment to increase and tighten it when inflation threatens. Of course, countercyclical policy does pose a danger of overreaction. If loose monetary policy seeking to end a recession goes too far, it may push aggregate demand so far to the right that it triggers inflation. If tight monetary policy seeking to reduce inflation goes too far, it may push aggregate demand so far to the left that a recession begins.  (a) summarizes the chain of effects that connect loose and tight monetary policy to changes in output and the price level.
p167.zh: 这些例子表明,货币政策应当具有反周期性;也就是说,它应当采取行动,抵消经济衰退和上升的商业周期。 当经济衰退导致失业增加时,美联储应该放松货币政策,并在通货膨胀威胁时收紧。 当然,反周期政策确实构成反应过度的危险。 如果寻求结束衰退的宽松货币政策走得太远,它可能会将迄今为止的总需求推向正确的方向,从而引发通货膨胀。 如果旨在降低通货膨胀的紧缩货币政策走得太远,那么它可能会将总需求推向左侧,从而导致衰退的开始。(a) 总结将松散和紧缩的货币政策与产出和价格水平变化联系起来的连锁效应。

p169.original: Federal Reserve Actions Over Last Four Decades
p169.zh: 过去四个十年的联邦储备行动

p170.original: For the period from 1970 through 2020, we can summarize Federal Reserve monetary policy by looking at how it targeted the federal funds interest rate using open market operations.
p170.zh: 从1970年到2020年,我们可以总结美联储的货币政策,看看它如何利用开放市场业务来针对联邦基金利率.

p171.original: Of course, telling the story of the U.S. economy since 1970 in terms of Federal Reserve actions leaves out many other macroeconomic factors that were influencing unemployment, recession, economic growth, and inflation over this time. The ten episodes of Federal Reserve action outlined in the sections below also demonstrate that we should consider the central bank as one of the leading actors influencing the macro economy. As we noted earlier, the single person with the greatest power to influence the U.S. economy is probably the Federal Reserve chairperson.
p171.zh: 当然,从1970年以来美国经济在美联储行动方面的故事中忽略了其他许多影响这段时间内失业、衰退、经济增长和通货膨胀的宏观经济因素。 以下各节概述的十集美联储行动也表明,我们应当把中央银行视为影响宏观经济的主要行为者之一。 正如我们先前指出的,影响美国经济权力最大的一个人可能是联邦储备委员会主席。

p172.original: shows how the Federal Reserve has carried out monetary policy by targeting the federal funds interest rate in the last few decades. The graph shows the federal funds interest rate (remember, this interest rate is set through open market operations), the unemployment rate, and the inflation rate since 1970. Different episodes of monetary policy during this period are indicated in the figure.
p172.zh: 说明美联储在过去几十年中如何通过针对联邦基金利率来实施货币政策. 该图显示了自1970年以来的联邦基金利率(记住,这一利率是通过开放市场运作设定的),失业率,以及通货膨胀率. 图中列出了这一期间不同的货币政策情况。

p173.zh: 货币政策、失业和通货膨胀

p175.original: Consider Episode 1 in the late 1970s. The rate of inflation was very high, exceeding 10% in 1979 and 1980, so the Federal Reserve used tight monetary policy to raise interest rates, with the federal funds rate rising from 5.5% in 1977 to 16.4% in 1981. By 1983, inflation was down to 3.2%, but aggregate demand contracted sharply enough that back-to-back recessions occurred in 1980 and in 1981–1982, and the unemployment rate rose from 5.8% in 1979 to 9.7% in 1982.
p175.zh: 20世纪70年代后期考虑第1集.通货膨胀率非常高,1979年和1980年超过10%,因此联邦储备局采用紧缩的货币政策提高利率,联邦基金利率从1977年的5.5%上升到1981年的16.4%. 到1983年,通货膨胀下降到3.2%,但总需求急剧萎缩,1980年和1981-1982年又发生衰退,失业率从1979年的5.8%上升到1982年的9.7%。

p177.original: In Episode 2, when economists persuaded the Federal Reserve in the early 1980s that inflation was declining, the Fed began slashing interest rates to reduce unemployment. The federal funds interest rate fell from 16.4% in 1981 to 6.8% in 1986. By 1986 or so, inflation had fallen to about 2% and the unemployment rate had come down to 7%, and was still falling.
p177.zh: 在第二集中,经济学家在20世纪80年代初说服美联储通货膨胀正在下降,美联储开始降低利率以减少失业.联邦基金利率从1981年的16.4%下降到1986年的6.8%. 到1986年左右,通货膨胀下降到约2%,失业率下降到7%,并且仍在下降。

p179.original: However, in Episode 3 in the late 1980s, inflation appeared to be creeping up again, rising from 2% in 1986 up toward 5% by 1989. In response, the Federal Reserve used contractionary monetary policy to raise the federal funds rates from 6.6% in 1987 to 9.2% in 1989. The tighter monetary policy stopped inflation, which fell from above 5% in 1990 to under 3% in 1992, but it also helped to cause the 1990-1991 recession, and the unemployment rate rose from 5.3% in 1989 to 7.5% by 1992.
p179.zh: 然而,在1980年代后期的第3集,通货膨胀似乎再次上升,从1986年的2%上升到1989年的5%。 作为回应,联邦储备局采用收缩性货币政策,将联邦资金利率从1987年的6.6%提高到1989年的9.2%。紧缩的货币政策制止了通货膨胀,通货膨胀从1990年的5%以上下降到1992年的3%以下,但也导致1990-1991年的衰退,失业率从1989年的5.3%上升到1992年的7.5%。

p181.original: In Episode 4, in the early 1990s, when the Federal Reserve was confident that inflation was back under control, it reduced interest rates, with the federal funds interest rate falling from 8.1% in 1990 to 3.5% in 1992. As the economy expanded, the unemployment rate declined from 7.5% in 1992 to less than 5% by 1997.
p181.zh: 第4集 1990年代初,当美联储相信通货膨胀已经恢复控制时,利率降低,联邦基金利率从1990年的8.1%下降到1992年的3.5%. 随着经济的发展,失业率从1992年的7.5%下降到1997年的5%以下。

p183.original: In Episodes 5 and 6, the Federal Reserve perceived a risk of inflation and raised the federal funds rate from 3% to 5.8% from 1993 to 1995. Inflation did not rise, and the period of economic growth during the 1990s continued. Then in 1999 and 2000, the Fed was concerned that inflation seemed to be creeping up so it raised the federal funds interest rate from 4.6% in December 1998 to 6.5% in June 2000. By early 2001, inflation was declining again, but a recession occurred in 2001. Between 2000 and 2002, the unemployment rate rose from 4.0% to 5.8%.
p183.zh: 第5集和第6集,联邦储备局认为存在通货膨胀风险,并从1993年至1995年将联邦资金利率从3%提高到5.8%。通货膨胀没有上升,1990年代的经济增长期仍在继续。之后在1999年和2000年,美联储担心通货膨胀似乎在上升,因此将联邦基金利率从1998年12月的4.6%提高到2000年6月的6.5%. 到2001年初,通货膨胀再次下降,但2001年出现了衰退。2000年至2002年,失业率从4.0%上升到5.8%。

p185.original: In Episodes 7 and 8, the Federal Reserve conducted a loose monetary policy and slashed the federal funds rate from 6.2% in 2000 to just 1.7% in 2002, and then again to 1% in 2003. They actually did this because of fear of Japan-style deflation. This persuaded them to lower the Fed funds further than they otherwise would have. The recession ended, but, unemployment rates were slow to decline in the early 2000s. Finally, in 2004, the unemployment rate declined and the Federal Reserve began to raise the federal funds rate until it reached 5% by 2007.
p185.zh: 第7集和第8集,联邦储备局实行宽松的货币政策,将联邦基金利率从2000年的6.2%降至2002年的1.7%,然后再次降至2003年的1%。 他们之所以这样做,其实是因为害怕日本式的通货紧缩。 这促使他们进一步降低美联储的资金,而不是他们本该降低的资金。衰退已经结束,但2000年代初失业率缓慢下降。 最后,2004年,失业率下降,联邦储备局开始提高联邦资金利率,直到2007年达到5%。

p187.original: In Episode 9, as the Great Recession took hold in 2008, the Federal Reserve was quick to slash interest rates, taking them down to 2% in 2008 and to nearly 0% in 2009. When the Fed had taken interest rates down to near-zero, the economy was still deep in recession. Open market operations could not make the interest rate turn negative. The Federal Reserve had to think “outside the box.”
p187.zh: 第9集是2008年大衰退时期,美联储迅速降低利率,2008年降至2%,2009年降至近0%。 当美联储将利率降到接近零时,经济仍然深陷衰退.开放市场的运作不能使利率变为负利率。美联储不得不考虑“箱外”的问题。

p189.original: In Episode 10, which started in March 2020, the Fed cut interest rates again, reducing the target federal funds rate from 2% to between 0–1/4% in a matter of weeks. Limited by the zero lower bound, the Fed once again had to think “outside the box” in order to further support the financial system.
p189.zh: 在2020年3月开始的第十集中,美联储再次削减利率,在几周内将目标联邦基金利率从2%降低到0–1/4%之间.美联储受到零下限的限制,不得不再次考虑“箱外”问题,以便进一步支持金融系统。

p190.original: The monetary policy discussed here is what was used prior to 2009. Go to this article on the Fed’s new monetary policy tools and this article on teaching the linkage between banks and the Fed for more information on modern monetary policy.
p190.zh: 本文讨论的货币政策是2009年之前采用的货币政策。 关于美联储新的货币政策工具的这篇文章和关于教育银行和美联储之间的联系的这篇文章,以了解更多关于现代货币政策的信息。

p192.original: An expansionary (or loose) monetary policy raises the quantity of money and credit above what it otherwise would have been and reduces interest rates, boosting aggregate demand, and thus countering recession. A contractionary monetary policy, also called a tight monetary policy, reduces the quantity of money and credit below what it otherwise would have been and raises interest rates, seeking to hold down inflation. During the 2008–2009 recession, central banks around the world also used quantitative easing to expand the supply of credit.
p192.zh: 扩张(或松散)的货币政策将货币和信贷的数量提高到本可以达到的水平,并降低利率,刺激总需求,从而应对衰退。紧缩的货币政策,也称紧缩的货币政策,将货币和信贷的数量降低到本来会达到的水平以下,并提高利率,试图抑制通货膨胀。 在2008-2009年经济衰退期间,世界各国中央银行也采用量化宽松来扩大信贷供应.

p194.original: Why does contractionary monetary policy cause interest rates to rise?
p194.zh: 收缩的货币政策为何导致利率上升?

p195.original: Contractionary policy reduces the amount of loanable funds in the economy. As with all goods, greater scarcity leads a greater price, so the interest rate, or the price of borrowing money, rises.
p195.zh: 承包政策减少经济中的可贷款资金数额.与所有商品一样,更加稀缺会导致更高的价格,因此利率,或借贷价格上升.

p196.original: Why does expansionary monetary policy causes interest rates to drop?
p196.zh: 扩张性货币政策为何导致利率下降?

p197.original: An increase in the amount of available loanable funds means that there are more people who want to lend. They, therefore, bid the price of borrowing (the interest rate) down.
p197.zh: 可贷款资金数额的增加意味着更多的人想要贷款。 因此,它们将借贷价格(利率)降低。

p199.original: How do the expansionary and contractionary monetary policy affect the quantity of money?
p199.zh: 扩张和收缩的货币政策如何影响货币数量?

p200.original: How do tight and loose monetary policy affect interest rates?
p200.zh: 紧缩和宽松的货币政策如何影响利率?

p201.original: How do expansionary, tight, contractionary, and loose monetary policy affect aggregate demand?
p201.zh: 扩张性、紧凑性、收缩性、宽松的货币政策如何影响总需求?

p202.original: Which kind of monetary policy would you expect in response to high inflation: expansionary or contractionary? Why?
p202.zh: 你期望什么样的货币政策来应对高通胀:扩张性还是收缩性? 为什么?

p203.original: Explain how to use quantitative easing to stimulate aggregate demand.
p203.zh: 解释如何利用量化宽松刺激总需求.

p205.original: A well-known economic model called the Phillips Curve (discussed in The Keynesian Perspective chapter) describes the short run tradeoff typically observed between inflation and unemployment. Based on the discussion of expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, explain why one of these variables usually falls when the other rises.
p205.zh: 一个著名的经济模式叫做菲利普斯曲线(The Keynesian Perspective chapter),描述了通常观察到的通货膨胀和失业之间的短径交易. 根据扩张和收缩货币政策的讨论,解释为什么其中一个变量通常在另一个变量上升时会下降.

p207.original: In the real world, effective monetary policy faces a number of significant hurdles. Monetary policy affects the economy only after a time lag that is typically long and of variable length. Remember, monetary policy involves a chain of events: the central bank must perceive a situation in the economy, hold a meeting, and make a decision to react by tightening or loosening monetary policy. The change in monetary policy must percolate through the banking system, changing the quantity of loans and affecting interest rates. When interest rates change, businesses must change their investment levels and consumers must change their borrowing patterns when purchasing homes or cars. Then it takes time for these changes to filter through the rest of the economy.
p207.zh: 在现实世界中,有效的货币政策面临若干重大障碍。货币政策只有在时间滞后之后才能影响经济,时间滞后通常很长,而且时间长短不定。记住,货币政策涉及一系列事件:中央银行必须了解经济形势,举行会议,并做出通过收紧或放松货币政策来做出反应的决定。货币政策的改变必须通过银行系统渗透,改变贷款数量,并影响利率。 当利率发生变化时,企业必须改变投资水平,消费者在购买房屋或汽车时必须改变借贷模式。 然后,这些变化需要时间才能渗透到经济的其余部分。

p208.original: As a result of this chain of events, monetary policy has little effect in the immediate future. Instead, its primary effects are felt perhaps one to three years in the future. The reality of long and variable time lags does not mean that a central bank should refuse to make decisions. It does mean that central banks should be humble about taking action, because of the risk that their actions can create as much or more economic instability as they resolve.
p208.zh: 由于这一连锁事件,货币政策在近期内没有什么效果. 相反,它的主要影响也许在将来一至三年内就感受到了。长期和可变时间滞后的现实并不意味着中央银行应拒绝作出决定。 这确实意味着中央银行应该谦卑地采取行动,因为其行动有可能造成经济不稳定的程度与它们所解决的程度相当或更多。

p210.original: Banks are legally required to hold a minimum level of reserves, but no rule prohibits them from holding additional excess reserves above the legally mandated limit. For example, during a recession banks may be hesitant to lend, because they fear that when the economy is contracting, a high proportion of loan applicants become less likely to repay their loans.
p210.zh: 银行在法律上必须持有最低水平的储备,但没有任何规则禁止它们持有超过法定限额的额外超额储备。 例如,在经济衰退期间,银行可能不愿贷款,因为他们担心当经济萎缩时,大量贷款申请者不太可能偿还贷款。

p211.original: When many banks are choosing to hold excess reserves, expansionary monetary policy may not work well. This may occur because the banks are concerned about a deteriorating economy, while the central bank is trying to expand the money supply. If the banks prefer to hold excess reserves above the legally required level, the central bank cannot force individual banks to make loans. Similarly, sensible businesses and consumers may be reluctant to borrow substantial amounts of money in a recession, because they recognize that firms’ sales and employees’ jobs are more insecure in a recession, and they do not want to face the need to make interest payments. The result is that during an especially deep recession, an expansionary monetary policy may have little effect on either the price level or the real GDP.
p211.zh: 当许多银行选择持有过剩的储备时,扩张性货币政策可能效果不佳.这可能是因为银行担心经济恶化,而中央银行则试图扩大货币供应。 如果银行倾向于持有超过法定水平的超额准备金,中央银行不能强迫个别银行提供贷款. 同样,明智的企业和消费者可能不愿意在衰退中借到大量资金,因为他们认识到,在衰退中,公司的销售和雇员的工作更加不安全,他们不想面对支付利息的需要。结果是,在特别严重的衰退期间,扩张性货币政策可能对价格水平或实际国内生产总值影响不大。

p212.original: Japan experienced this situation in the 1990s and early 2000s. Japan’s economy entered a period of very slow growth, dipping in and out of recession, in the early 1990s. By February 1999, the Bank of Japan had lowered the equivalent of its federal funds rate to 0%. It kept it there most of the time through 2003. Moreover, in the two years from March 2001 to March 2003, the Bank of Japan also expanded the country's money supply by about 50%—an enormous increase. Even this highly expansionary monetary policy, however, had no substantial effect on stimulating aggregate demand. Japan’s economy continued to experience extremely slow growth into the mid-2000s.
p212.zh: 1990年代和2000年代初,日本经历了这种情况。 日本经济在1990年代初进入了非常缓慢的增长、衰退的时期。 到1999年2月,日本银行已经将其联邦基金利率的等值降低到0%.大部分时间它都保存在那里,直到2003年. 此外,在2001年3月至2003年3月的两年中,日本银行还大幅度地扩大了该国货币供应,大约增加了50美元。 然而,即使是这种高度扩张的货币政策,也没有对刺激总需求产生实质性影响。2000年代中期,日本经济继续出现极其缓慢的增长。

p213.original: Should monetary policy decisions be made more democratically?
p213.zh: 货币政策决定是否应该更加民主?

p214.original: Should a nation’s Congress or legislature comprised of elected representatives conduct monetary policy or should a politically appointed central bank that is more independent of voters take charge? Here are some of the arguments.
p214.zh: 一个国家的国会或由民选代表组成的立法机构应该实行货币政策,还是应该由政治任命的、更独立于选民的中央银行来管理? 以下是一些论点。

p215.original: The Case for Greater Democratic Control of Monetary Policy
p215.zh: 对货币政策实行更大民主控制的理由

p216.original: Elected representatives pass taxes and spending bills to conduct fiscal policy by passing tax and spending bills. They could handle monetary policy in the same way. They will sometimes make mistakes, but in a democracy, it is better to have elected officials who are accountable to voters make mistakes instead of political appointees. After all, the people appointed to the top governing positions at the Federal Reserve—and to most central banks around the world—are typically bankers and economists. They are not representatives of borrowers like small businesses or farmers nor are they representatives of labor unions. Central banks might not be so quick to raise interest rates if they had to pay more attention to firms and people in the real economy.
p216.zh: 当选代表通过税收和支出法案,通过税收和支出法案来实施财政政策. 它们可以同样的方式处理货币政策。 他们有时会犯错误,但是在一个民主国家,最好让那些对选民负责的民选官员犯错误,而不是政治任命。毕竟,被任命担任美联储最高领导职务的人——以及全世界大多数中央银行——通常是银行家和经济学家。 她们不是小企业或农民等借款人的代表,也不是工会的代表。 如果中央银行必须更多地关注实体经济中的公司和人民,它们可能不会那么迅速地提高利率。

p217.original: The Case for an Independent Central Bank

p218.original: Because the central bank has some insulation from day-to-day politics, its members can take a nonpartisan look at specific economic situations and make tough, immediate decisions when necessary. The idea of giving a legislature the ability to create money and hand out loans is likely to end up badly, sooner or later. It is simply too tempting for lawmakers to expand the money supply to fund their projects. The long term result will be rampant inflation. Also, a central bank, acting according to the laws passed by elected officials, can respond far more quickly than a legislature. For example, the U.S. budget takes months to debate, pass, and sign into law, but monetary policy decisions happen much more rapidly. Day-to-day democratic control of monetary policy is impractical and seems likely to lead to an overly expansionary monetary policy and higher inflation.
p218.zh: 因为中央银行与日常政治有一定隔绝性,其成员可以无党派地审视具体的经济状况,必要时立即作出艰难的决定.赋予立法机构创造资金和发放贷款的能力这一想法,迟早可能会出现糟糕的结局。立法者扩大资金供应,为其项目提供资金,实在太诱人了。长期结果是通货膨胀猖獗。 此外,中央银行根据民选官员通过的法律采取行动,其反应速度比立法机构快得多。 例如,美国的预算需要几个月的时间来辩论、通过和签署法律,但货币政策决定的发生要快得多。 对货币政策的日常民主控制是不切实际的,似乎可能导致过度扩张的货币政策和更高的通货膨胀。

p219.original: The problem of excess reserves does not affect contractionary policy. Central bankers have an old saying that monetary policy can be like pulling and pushing on a string: when the central bank pulls on the string and uses contractionary monetary policy, it can definitely raise interest rates and reduce aggregate demand. However, when the central bank tries to push on the string of expansionary monetary policy, the string may sometimes just fold up limp and have little effect, because banks decide not to loan out their excess reserves. Do not take this analogy too literally—expansionary monetary policy usually does have real effects, after that inconveniently long and variable lag. There are also times, like Japan’s economy in the late 1990s and early 2000s, when expansionary monetary policy has been insufficient to lift a recession-prone economy.
p219.zh: 储备过剩问题不影响收缩政策.中央银行家有一句古老的谚语,认为货币政策可以像拉拉拉拉一样,像拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉拉 然而,当中央银行试图推行扩张性货币政策时,该弦有时可能只是折叠而无效果,因为银行决定不贷款出其多余的储备. 不要太从字面上作这种类比——扩张的货币政策通常在这种不方便的漫长和可变的滞后之后确实产生实际影响。也有的时候,如1990年代末和2000年代初的日本经济,扩张性的货币政策不足以解除容易陷入衰退的经济。

p220.zh: 速度的不可预测的移动

p221.original: Velocity is a term that economists use to describe how quickly money circulates through the economy. We define the velocity of money in a year as:
p221.zh: 高速是一个经济学家用来描述货币在经济中流通速度的术语. 我们把一年内货币的速度定义为:

p222.original: Specific measurements of velocity depend on the definition of the money supply used. Consider the velocity of M1, the total amount of currency in circulation and checking account balances. In 2009, for example, M1 was $1.7 trillion and nominal GDP was $14.3 trillion, so the velocity of M1 was 8.4 (which is $14.3 trillion/$1.7 trillion). A higher velocity of money means that the average dollar circulates more times in a year. A lower velocity means that the average dollar circulates fewer times in a year.
p222.zh: 速度的具体衡量取决于所用货币供应的定义。考虑M1的速度,流通货币总额和账户余额的核对。 例如,2009年,M1为1.7万亿美元,名义GDP为14.3万亿美元,因此M1的速度为8.4(14.3万亿美元/1.7万亿美元).货币速度的提高意味着平均美元在一年中的流通次数增加。速度较低意味着平均美元在一年内的流通次数较少。

p223.original: See the following Clear It Up feature for a discussion of how deflation could affect monetary policy.
p223.zh: 关于通货紧缩如何影响货币政策的讨论,见下面的Clear It Up 特征。

p224.original: What happens during episodes of deflation?
p224.zh: 通货紧缩时会发生什么?

p225.original: Deflation occurs when the rate of inflation is negative; that is, instead of money having less purchasing power over time, as occurs with inflation, money is worth more. Deflation can make it very difficult for monetary policy to address a recession.
p225.zh: 当通货膨胀率为负值时,就会出现通货紧缩;也就是说,货币的购买力会随着时间推移而降低,而不是随着通货膨胀而降低,而货币的价值会更高。通货紧缩可能使货币政策很难应对衰退。

p226.original: Remember that the real interest rate is the nominal interest rate minus the rate of inflation. If the nominal interest rate is 7% and the rate of inflation is 3%, then the borrower is effectively paying a 4% real interest rate. If the nominal interest rate is 7% and there is deflation of 2%, then the real interest rate is actually 9%. In this way, an unexpected deflation raises the real interest payments for borrowers. It can lead to a situation where borrowers do not repay an unexpectedly high number of loans, and banks find that their net worth is decreasing or negative. When banks are suffering losses, they become less able and eager to make new loans. Aggregate demand declines, which can lead to recession.
p226.zh: 记住,实际利率是名义利率减去通货膨胀率。 如果名义利率为7%,通货膨胀率为3%,那么借款人实际上支付4%的实际利率. 如果名义利率为7%,而通货紧缩为2%,那么实际利率实际上是9%。 这样,意外的通货紧缩提高了借款人的实际利息支付额。 这可能导致借款人不偿还出乎意料的巨额贷款,银行发现其净值正在下降或负值. 当银行遭受损失时,它们变得不太有能力,更渴望提供新的贷款。需求总量下降,可能导致衰退。

p227.original: Then the double-whammy: After causing a recession, deflation can make it difficult for monetary policy to work. Say that the central bank uses expansionary monetary policy to reduce the nominal interest rate all the way to zero—but the economy has 5% deflation. As a result, the real interest rate is 5%, and because a central bank cannot make the nominal interest rate negative, expansionary policy cannot reduce the real interest rate further.
p227.zh: 接下来的双错:通货紧缩导致衰退后,货币政策可能难以奏效.说央行使用扩张性货币政策将名义利率一路降低到零,但经济有5%的通货紧缩. 因此,实际利率为5%,由于中央银行不能使名义利率为负,扩张政策不能进一步降低实际利率.

p228.original: In the U.S. economy during the early 1930s, deflation was 6.7% per year from 1930–1933, which caused many borrowers to default on their loans and many banks to end up bankrupt, which in turn contributed substantially to the Great Depression. Not all episodes of deflation, however, end in economic depression. Japan, for example, experienced deflation of slightly less than 1% per year from 1999–2002, which hurt the Japanese economy, but it still grew by about 0.9% per year over this period. There is at least one historical example of deflation coexisting with rapid growth. The U.S. economy experienced deflation of about 1.1% per year over the quarter-century from 1876–1900, but real GDP also expanded at a rapid clip of 4% per year over this time, despite some occasional severe recessions.
p228.zh: 1930年代初期的美国经济中,通货紧缩从1930–1933年每年达到6.7 %,这导致许多借款人拖欠贷款,许多银行最终破产,这反过来又对大萧条做出了实质性贡献. 然而,并非所有的通货紧缩事件都以经济萧条为终点。 例如,日本从1999-2002年起每年的通货紧缩略低于1%,这伤害了日本的经济,但在此期间,每年的通货紧缩仍增长约0.9 % 。 至少有一个历史上的通货紧缩与快速增长共存的例子。 美国经济从1876年到1900年的25年里每年通缩约1.1%,但实际GDP在这一时期也以每年4%的速率增长,尽管偶尔会出现严重的衰退。

p229.original: The central bank should be on guard against deflation and, if necessary, use expansionary monetary policy to prevent any long-lasting or extreme deflation from occurring. Except in severe cases like the Great Depression, deflation does not guarantee economic disaster.
p229.zh: 中央银行应防范通货紧缩,必要时采用扩张性货币政策,防止任何长期或极端通货紧缩的发生。 除大萧条等严重情况外,通货紧缩并不能保证经济灾难.

p231.original: Recall from The Macroeconomic Perspective that

p233.original: We sometimes call this equation the basic quantity equation of money but, as you can see, it is just the definition of velocity written in a different form. This equation must hold true, by definition.
p233.zh: 我们有时把这个方程称为金钱的基本数量方程,但是,如你所见,它只是用不同的形式写成的速度的定义.顾名思义,这一方程式必须正确。

p234.original: If velocity is constant over time, then a certain percentage rise in the money supply on the left-hand side of the basic quantity equation of money will inevitably lead to the same percentage rise in nominal GDP—although this change could happen through an increase in inflation, or an increase in real GDP, or some combination of the two. If velocity is changing over time but in a constant and predictable way, then changes in the money supply will continue to have a predictable effect on nominal GDP. If velocity changes unpredictably over time, however, then the effect of changes in the money supply on nominal GDP becomes unpredictable.
p234.zh: 如果速度随时间而保持不变,那么货币基本数量方程左侧的货币供应量就会有一定百分比的上升,不可避免地导致名义GDP的同样百分比的上升——尽管这种变化可能通过通货膨胀的上升,或实际GDP的增加,或两者的某种组合来实现. 如果速度随着时间而变化,但以持续和可预测的方式变化,那么货币供应的变化将继续对名义国内生产总值产生可预测的影响。 然而,如果速度在一段时间内变化不可预测,那么货币供应的变化对名义国内总产值的影响就变得难以预测。

p235.original: illustrates the actual velocity of money in the U.S. economy as measured by using M1, the most common definition of the money supply. From 1960 up to about 1980, velocity appears fairly predictable; that is, it is increasing at a fairly constant rate. In the early 1980s, however, velocity as calculated with M1 becomes more variable. The reasons for these sharp changes in velocity remain a puzzle. Economists suspect that the changes in velocity are related to innovations in banking and finance which have changed how we are using money in making economic transactions: for example, the growth of electronic payments; a rise in personal borrowing and credit card usage; and accounts that make it easier for people to hold money in savings accounts, where it is counted as M2, right up to the moment that they want to write a check on the money and transfer it to M1. So far at least, it has proven difficult to draw clear links between these kinds of factors and the specific up-and-down fluctuations in M1. Given many changes in banking and the prevalence of electronic banking, economists now favor M2 as a measure of money rather than the narrower M1.
p235.zh: 说明美国经济中货币的实际速度,用最常用的货币供应定义M1来衡量。 从1960年到1980年左右,速度似乎相当可以预测;也就是说,速度正在以相当恒定的速度增长。 然而在1980年代初期,用M1计算的速度变得更加可变.速度发生这些急剧变化的原因仍然是一个谜题。经济学家怀疑速度的变化与银行和金融的创新有关,这些创新改变了我们如何利用资金进行经济交易:例如,电子支付的增长;个人借贷和信用卡使用率的提高;以及使人们更容易在储蓄账户中持有资金的账户,在那里被算作M2,直到他们想写一张钱的支票并将其转至M1时为止. 至少到目前为止,事实证明很难在这些因素与M1的具体上下波动之间建立明确的联系。 鉴于银行业的许多变化和电子银行业的盛行,经济学家现在倾向于将M2作为货币衡量标准,而不是狭隘的M1.

p236.zh: 使用 M1 计算速度

p237.zh: 使用 M1 计算速度

p238.original: In the 1970s, when velocity as measured by M1 seemed predictable, a number of economists, led by Nobel laureate Milton Friedman (1912–2006), argued that the best monetary policy was for the central bank to increase the money supply at a constant growth rate. These economists argued that with the long and variable lags of monetary policy, and the political pressures on central bankers, central bank monetary policies were as likely to have undesirable as to have desirable effects. Thus, these economists believed that the monetary policy should seek steady growth in the money supply of 3% per year. They argued that a steady monetary growth rate would be correct over longer time periods, since it would roughly match the growth of the real economy. In addition, they argued that giving the central bank less discretion to conduct monetary policy would prevent an overly activist central bank from becoming a source of economic instability and uncertainty. In this spirit, Friedman wrote in 1967: “The first and most important lesson that history teaches about what monetary policy can do—and it is a lesson of the most profound importance—is that monetary policy can prevent money itself from being a major source of economic disturbance.”
p238.zh: 在20世纪70年代,当以M1衡量的速度似乎可以预测时,一些经济学家在诺贝尔奖得主米尔顿·弗里德曼(1912–2006)的带领下认为,最好的货币政策是中央银行以恒定的增长率增加货币供应. 这些经济学家认为,由于货币政策长期和可变的滞后以及对中央银行家的政治压力,中央银行的货币政策很可能不可取,甚至产生理想的效果。 因此,这些经济学家认为,货币政策应该寻求每年3%的货币供应稳步增长。 他们认为,在较长的时期内,稳定的货币增长率是正确的,因为它与实体经济的增长大致相符。 此外,他们认为,给予中央银行较少的采取货币政策的酌处权,将防止过度活跃的中央银行成为经济不稳定和不确定的根源。本着这种精神,弗里德曼在1967年写道 : “ 历史上第一个最重要的教训是货币政策可以做什么,这是最重要的教训,那就是货币政策能够防止货币本身成为经济动荡的一个主要来源。 ”

p239.original: As the velocity of M1 began to fluctuate in the 1980s, having the money supply grow at a predetermined and unchanging rate seemed less desirable, because as the quantity theory of money shows, the combination of constant growth in the money supply and fluctuating velocity would cause nominal GDP to rise and fall in unpredictable ways. The jumpiness of velocity in the 1980s caused many central banks to focus less on the rate at which the quantity of money in the economy was increasing, and instead to set monetary policy by reacting to whether the economy was experiencing or in danger of higher inflation or unemployment.
p239.zh: 随着M1的速度在20世纪80年代开始波动,货币供应以预先确定和不变的速度增长似乎不那么可取,因为货币供应量理论表明,货币供应的恒定增长和波动速度的结合将导致名义GDP以不可预测的方式上升和下降。20世纪80年代速度的飞跃,使得许多中央银行对经济中货币数量增长的速度的注意较少,而是通过对经济是否正在经历或面临通货膨胀或失业上升的危险作出反应来制定货币政策.

p241.original: If you were to survey central bankers around the world and ask them what they believe should be the primary task of monetary policy, the most popular answer by far would be fighting inflation. Most central bankers believe that the neoclassical model of economics accurately represents the economy over the medium to long term. Remember that in the neoclassical model of the economy, we draw the aggregate supply curve as a vertical line at the level of potential GDP, as  shows. In the neoclassical model, economists determine the level of potential GDP (and the natural rate of unemployment that exists when the economy is producing at potential GDP) by real economic factors. If the original level of aggregate demand is AD0, then an expansionary monetary policy that shifts aggregate demand to AD1 only creates an inflationary increase in the price level, but it does not alter GDP or unemployment. From this perspective, all that monetary policy can do is to lead to low inflation or high inflation—and low inflation provides a better climate for a healthy and growing economy. After all, low inflation means that businesses making investments can focus on real economic issues, not on figuring out ways to protect themselves from the costs and risks of inflation. In this way, a consistent pattern of low inflation can contribute to long-term growth.
p241.zh: 如果你调查全世界的中央银行家,问他们认为什么应该是货币政策的首要任务,那么迄今为止最受欢迎的答案就是与通货膨胀作斗争. 大多数中央银行家认为,经济学的新古典主义模式准确地代表了中长期的经济.记住,在新古典主义的经济模式中,我们绘制总供给曲线,作为潜在GDP水平的垂直线,如所示. 在新古典主义模式中,经济学家通过实际经济因素确定潜在的GDP水平(以及当经济在潜在的GDP生产时存在的自然失业率). 如果最初的总需求水平是AD0,那么将总需求转向AD1的扩张性货币政策只会造成物价水平的通货膨胀上升,但不会改变GDP或失业. 从这个角度看,货币政策所能做的只是导致低通货膨胀或高通货膨胀,而低通货膨胀为健康和增长的经济提供了更好的环境。毕竟,低通胀意味着投资的企业可以专注于实际经济问题,而不是想出保护自己免受通货膨胀成本和风险的方法. 这样,持续的低通货膨胀模式可以促进长期增长。

p242.original: Monetary Policy in a Neoclassical Model
p242.zh: 新古典主义模式中的货币政策

p243.original: This vision of focusing monetary policy on a low rate of inflation is so attractive that many countries have rewritten their central banking laws since in the 1990s to have their bank practice inflation targeting, which means that the central bank is legally required to focus primarily on keeping inflation low. By 2014, central banks in 28 countries, including Austria, Brazil, Canada, Israel, Korea, Mexico, New Zealand, Spain, Sweden, Thailand, and the United Kingdom faced a legal requirement to target the inflation rate. A notable exception is the Federal Reserve in the United States, which does not practice inflation-targeting. Instead, the law governing the Federal Reserve requires it to take both unemployment and inflation into account.
p243.zh: 这种将货币政策的重点放在低通货膨胀率上的构想非常有吸引力,以至于许多国家自1990年代以来就重新制定了中央银行法,使其银行采用针对通货膨胀的做法,这意味着中央银行在法律上必须主要侧重于保持低通货膨胀率。 到2014年,奥地利,巴西,加拿大,以色列,韩国,墨西哥,新西兰,西班牙,瑞典,泰国,英国等28个国家的中央银行都面临着针对通胀率的法律要求. 一个显著的例外是美国的联邦储备局,它不实行通货膨胀目标。 相反,管辖联邦储备局的法律要求它既考虑到失业问题,也考虑到通货膨胀问题。

p244.original: Economists have no final consensus on whether a central bank should be required to focus only on inflation or should have greater discretion. For those who subscribe to the inflation targeting philosophy, the fear is that politicians who are worried about slow economic growth and unemployment will constantly pressure the central bank to conduct a loose monetary policy—even if the economy is already producing at potential GDP. In some countries, the central bank may lack the political power to resist such pressures, with the result of higher inflation, but no long-term reduction in unemployment. The U.S. Federal Reserve has a tradition of independence, but central banks in other countries may be under greater political pressure. For all of these reasons—long and variable lags, excess reserves, unstable velocity, and controversy over economic goals—monetary policy in the real world is often difficult. The basic message remains, however, that central banks can affect aggregate demand through the conduct of monetary policy and in that way influence macroeconomic outcomes.
p244.zh: 经济学家对于中央银行是否应当只关注通货膨胀或应当有更大的酌处权没有最后的共识.对于那些赞同通货膨胀目标哲学的人来说,担心担心经济增长缓慢和失业的政客会不断向中央银行施压,迫使其采取宽松的货币政策——即使经济已经在生产潜在的国内生产总值。 在一些国家,中央银行可能缺乏抵御这种压力的政治权力,导致通货膨胀上升,但失业不会长期减少。 美国.美联储有独立的传统,但其他国家的中央银行可能会受到更大的政治压力. 由于所有这些原因——长期和可变的滞后、过剩的储备、不稳定的速度和对经济目标的争议——现实世界的货币政策往往很困难。 然而,基本的信息仍然是,中央银行可通过货币政策影响总需求,从而影响宏观经济结果。

p246.original: One long-standing concern about having the central bank focus on inflation and unemployment is that it may be overlooking certain other economic problems that are coming in the future. For example, from 1994 to 2000 during what was known as the “dot-com” boom, the U.S. stock market, which the Dow Jones Industrial Index measures (which includes 30 very large companies from across the U.S. economy), nearly tripled in value. The Nasdaq index, which includes many smaller technology companies, increased in value by a multiple of five from 1994 to 2000. These rates of increase were clearly not sustainable. Stock values as measured by the Dow Jones were almost 20% lower in 2009 than they had been in 2000. Stock values in the Nasdaq index were 50% lower in 2009 than they had been in 2000. The drop-off in stock market values contributed to the 2001 recession and the higher unemployment that followed.
p246.zh: 中央银行一直关注通货膨胀和失业问题,人们担心这一问题,认为它可能忽略了今后将出现的某些其他经济问题。 例如,从1994年到2000年,在所谓的“dot-com”繁荣时期,美国股票市场,即道琼斯工业指数(包括来自全美国经济的30个非常大公司)衡量的股票市场,其价值几乎增加了两倍。纳斯达克指数包括许多较小的技术公司,从1994年至2000年,其价值增加了五倍。 这些增长率显然是不可持续的。2009年,道琼斯公司测得的股票价值比2000年低近20%。2009年,纳斯达克指数中的股票价值比2000年低50%。股票市场价值的下跌导致2001年的衰退和随后的高失业率。

p247.original: We can tell a similar story about housing prices in the mid-2000s. During the 1970s, 1980s, and 1990s, housing prices increased at about 6% per year on average. During what came to be known as the “housing bubble” from 2003 to 2005, housing prices increased at almost double this annual rate. These rates of increase were clearly not sustainable. When housing prices fell in 2007 and 2008, many banks and households found that their assets were worth less than they expected, which contributed to the recession that started in 2007.
p247.zh: 我们可以讲述一个类似的故事,说明2000年代中期的住房价格。 在1970年代、1980年代和1990年代,住房价格平均每年上涨6%左右。 在2003年至2005年期间被称为“住房泡沫”期间,住房价格几乎是这一年增长率的两倍。 这些增长率显然是不可持续的。2007年和2008年,当住房价格下跌时,许多银行和家庭发现其资产价值低于预期,这导致了2007年开始的衰退。

p248.original: At a broader level, some economists worry about a leverage cycle, where “leverage” is a term financial economists use to mean “borrowing.” When economic times are good, banks and the financial sector are eager to lend, and people and firms are eager to borrow. Remember that a money multiplier determines the amount of money and credit in an economy —a process of loans made, money deposited, and more loans made. In good economic times, this surge of lending exaggerates the episode of economic growth. It can even be part of what lead prices of certain assets—like stock prices or housing prices—to rise at unsustainably high annual rates. At some point, when economic times turn bad, banks and the financial sector become much less willing to lend, and credit becomes expensive or unavailable to many potential borrowers. The sharp reduction in credit, perhaps combined with the deflating prices of a dot-com stock price bubble or a housing bubble, makes the economic downturn worse than it would otherwise be.
p248.zh: 在更广泛的层面上,一些经济学家担心杠杆周期,金融经济学家用“杠杆”一词来表示“借款 ” 。 当经济时代好的时候,银行和金融部门急于贷款,而人们和公司急于借款。记住,一个货币乘数决定了经济中货币和信贷的数额——一个贷款、存款和更多贷款的过程。 在良好的经济时代,这种贷款的激增夸大了经济增长的一幕.某些资产的主要价格——如股票价格或住房价格——甚至有可能以不可持续的高年利率上涨。 在经济时代变得糟糕的某一时刻,银行和金融部门更不愿意贷款,许多潜在借款人也变得昂贵或得不到信贷。信贷的急剧下降,也许再加上一个点-公司股价泡沫或一个住房泡沫的物价下跌,使得经济下滑比本来会更糟糕。

p249.original: Thus, some economists have suggested that the central bank should not just look at economic growth, inflation, and unemployment rates, but should also keep an eye on asset prices and leverage cycles. Such proposals are quite controversial. If a central bank had announced in 1997 that stock prices were rising “too fast” or in 2004 that housing prices were rising “too fast,” and then taken action to hold down price increases, many people and their elected political representatives would have been outraged. Neither the Federal Reserve nor any other central banks want to take the responsibility of deciding when stock prices and housing prices are too high, too low, or just right. As further research explores how asset price bubbles and leverage cycles can affect an economy, central banks may need to think about whether they should conduct monetary policy in a way that would seek to moderate these effects.
p249.zh: 因此,一些经济学家建议,中央银行不应仅仅关注经济增长、通货膨胀和失业率,还应关注资产价格和杠杆周期。此类建议颇具争议。 如果一中央银行在1997年宣布股票价格“过快”上涨,或2004年宣布住房价格“过快”上涨,然后采取行动压低价格上涨,许多人及其当选的政治代表就会感到愤怒。美联储和任何其他中央银行都不愿承担责任,决定股票价格和房价何时过高,太低,或是否正确. 在进一步研究资产价格泡沫和杠杆周期如何影响经济时,中央银行可能需要考虑它们是否应该以设法减轻这些影响的方式实施货币政策。

p250.original: Let’s end this chapter with a Work it Out exercise in how the Fed—or any central bank—would stir up the economy by increasing the money supply.
p250.zh: 以美联储(或任何中央银行)如何通过增加货币供应来刺激经济的工作结束这一章。

p257.original: The Problem of the Zero Percent Interest Rate Lower Bound

p258.original: In 2008, the U.S. Federal Reserve found itself in a difficult position. The federal funds rate was on its way to near zero, which meant that traditional open market operations, by which the Fed purchases U.S. Treasury Bills to lower short term interest rates, was no longer viable. This so called “zero bound problem,” prompted the Fed, under then Chair Ben Bernanke, to attempt some unconventional policies, collectively called quantitative easing. By early 2014, quantitative easing nearly quintupled the amount of bank reserves. This likely contributed to the U.S. economy’s recovery, but the impact was muted, probably due to some of the hurdles mentioned in the last section of this module.  The unprecedented increase in bank reserves also led to fears of inflation, which never bore out. Throughout the 2010s there have been no serious signs of inflation with core inflation around a stable 1.5–2%. As of early 2015, however, there have been no serious signs of a boom, with core inflation around a stable 1.7%.
p258.zh: 2008年,美国.美联储发现自己处境困难.联邦基金利率正走向接近零,这意味着美联储通过这种传统的开放市场业务购买美国.降低短期利率的国库券已不再可行。 这所谓的“零约束问题”促使美联储在当时的主席本·伯南克的领导下尝试一些非常规政策,统称为量化宽松。 到2014年初,量化宽松几乎使银行储备额增加了五倍. 这可能会促进美国经济的复苏,但影响没有受到任何影响,这可能是由于本单元最后一节中提到的一些障碍。银行储备的空前增加也导致人们担心通货膨胀,而通货膨胀从未消除。整个2010年代,没有严重的通货膨胀迹象,核心通胀率稳定在1.5-2 %左右。 然而,截至2015年初,没有出现严重繁荣的迹象,核心通胀率稳定在1.7%左右.

p259.original: The Zero Lower Bound was encountered again in 2020 due to the pandemic, when the target federal funds rate dropped by over two percentage points in a matter of weeks. The Fed further responded by increasing asset purchases by an even greater amount, and at a faster rate, than in 2009. When the U.S. started experiencing higher-than-average inflation in 2021, the Fed chair Jerome Powell responded to criticisms by saying that the Fed was poised to consider rate increases and start tapering the rate of asset purchases into 2022. It remains to be seen whether inflation can be tamed moving forward, or if more aggressive policy measures will be required.
p259.zh: 2020年,由于这一大流行病,联邦目标资金率在几周内下降了两个百分点以上,因此再次遇到了 " 零下限 " 。美联储还作出进一步回应,将资产购买量比2009年增加甚至更多,速度更快。 当美国在2021年开始经历高于平均水平的通货膨胀时,美联储主席杰罗姆·鲍威尔回应批评说,美联储准备考虑利率上升,并开始将资产购买率压入2022年.能否遏制通货膨胀,或者是否需要采取更积极的政策措施,尚有待观察。

p261.original: Monetary policy is inevitably imprecise, for a number of reasons: (a) the effects occur only after long and variable lags; (b) if banks decide to hold excess reserves, monetary policy cannot force them to lend; and (c) velocity may shift in unpredictable ways. The basic quantity equation of money is MV = PQ, where M is the money supply, V is the velocity of money, P is the price level, and Q is the real output of the economy. Some central banks, like the European Central Bank, practice inflation targeting, which means that the only goal of the central bank is to keep inflation within a low target range. Other central banks, such as the U.S. Federal Reserve, are free to focus on either reducing inflation or stimulating an economy that is in recession, whichever goal seems most important at the time.
p261.zh: 货币政策不可避免地是不准确的,原因如下:(a) 只有在长期和可变的滞后之后才会产生影响;(b) 如果银行决定持有过多的储备,货币政策不能强迫它们贷款;(c) 速度可能以无法预测的方式转变。货币的基本量方程为MV = PQ,其中M是货币供给,V是货币速度,P是价格水平,Q是经济的实际产出. 一些中央银行,如欧洲中央银行,实行通货膨胀目标,这意味着中央银行的唯一目标是将通货膨胀保持在低目标范围内. 其他中央银行,如美国.美联储可以自由地专注于减少通货膨胀或刺激处于衰退中的经济体,以当时看来最重要的目标为准。

p263.original: Why might banks want to hold excess reserves in time of recession?
p263.zh: 银行为何想在经济衰退时持有过剩的储备?

p264.original: In times of economic uncertainty, banks may worry that borrowers will lose the ability to repay their loans. They may also fear that a panic is more likely and they will need the excess reserves to meet their obligations.
p264.zh: 在经济不确定的时候,银行可能会担心借款人会失去偿还贷款的能力. 他们还可能担心恐慌的可能性更大,他们需要多余的储备来履行义务。

p265.original: Why might the velocity of money change unexpectedly?
p265.zh: 为什么金钱的速度会出乎意料地改变?

p266.original: If consumer optimism changes, spending can speed up or slow down. This could also happen in a case where consumers need to buy a large number of items quickly, such as in a situation of national emergency.
p266.zh: 如果消费者乐观态度发生变化,支出可以加快或放慢. 在消费者需要迅速购买大量物品的情况下,例如在国家紧急状态下,也可能出现这种情况。

c4.original: The original equilibrium occurs at E0. An expansionary monetary policy will shift the supply of loanable funds to the right from the original supply curve (S0) to the new supply curve (S1) and to a new equilibrium of E1, reducing the interest rate from 8% to 6%. A contractionary monetary policy will shift the supply of loanable funds to the left from the original supply curve (S0) to the new supply (S2), and raise the interest rate from 8% to 10%.
c4.zh: 原平衡发生在E0.扩张性的货币政策将把可贷款资金的供应从原来的供给曲线(S0)向右转向新的供给曲线(S1),并将利率从8%降至6%。收缩性货币政策将把可贷资金的供应从原来的供给曲线(S0)转向新的供给曲线(S2),并将利率从8%提高到10%.

c5.original: (a) The economy is originally in a recession with the equilibrium output and price shown at E0. Expansionary monetary policy will reduce interest rates and shift aggregate demand to the right from AD0 to AD1, leading to the new equilibrium (E1) at the potential GDP level of output with a relatively small rise in the price level. (b) The economy is originally producing above the potential GDP level of output at the equilibrium E0 and is experiencing pressures for an inflationary rise in the price level. Contractionary monetary policy will shift aggregate demand to the left from AD0 to AD1, thus leading to a new equilibrium (E1) at the potential GDP level of output.
c5.zh: (a) 经济最初处于衰退状态,平衡产出和价格为E0。扩大的货币政策将降低利率,将总需求从AD0转向AD1,从而在潜在的国内生产总值水平上实现新的平衡(E1),价格水平也略有上升。(b) 经济最初在E0平衡值时产量高于潜在国内总产值水平,并面临物价上涨的压力。收缩性货币政策将把总需求从AD0转向AD1,从而在潜在的国内生产总值产出水平上实现新的平衡(E1)。

c6.original: (a) In expansionary monetary policy the central bank causes the supply of money and loanable funds to increase, which lowers the interest rate, stimulating additional borrowing for investment and consumption, and shifting aggregate demand right. The result is a higher price level and, at least in the short run, higher real GDP. (b) In contractionary monetary policy, the central bank causes the supply of money and credit in the economy to decrease, which raises the interest rate, discouraging borrowing for investment and consumption, and shifting aggregate demand left. The result is a lower price level and, at least in the short run, lower real GDP.
c6.zh: (a) 在扩张性货币政策中,中央银行促使货币和可贷款资金的供应增加,从而降低了利率,刺激了更多的投资和消费借款,并转移了总需求权。其结果是物价水平提高,至少在短期内,实际国内生产总值也提高。(b) 在收缩性货币政策中,中央银行造成经济中货币和信贷供应减少,这提高了利率,抑制了为投资和消费而借贷,并改变了剩下的总需求。其结果是物价水平降低,至少在短期内实际国内总产值下降。

c7.original: Through the episodes here, the Federal Reserve typically reacted to higher inflation with a contractionary monetary policy and a higher interest rate, and reacted to higher unemployment with an expansionary monetary policy and a lower interest rate.
c7.zh: 美联储通过这里的事件,通常会以收缩的货币政策和较高的利率对较高的通货膨胀作出反应,并以扩张的货币政策和较低的利率对较高的失业率作出反应。

c8.original: Velocity is the nominal GDP divided by the money supply for a given year. We can calculate different measures of velocity by using different measures of the money supply. Velocity, as calculated by using M1, has lacked a steady trend since the 1980s, instead bouncing up and down. Note also that the redefinition of M1 to include savings deposits in 2020 (see Money and Banking) drastically increased M1 in 2020, causing velocity to plummet. (credit: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)
c8.zh: 速率是特定年份货币供应除以名义GDP. 我们可以通过使用不同量度的货币供应来计算不同的速度度量.使用M1计算出的高速自1980年代以来缺乏稳定趋势,反而上下起伏。还注意到,M1的重新定义将2020年的储蓄存款包括在内(见货币和银行业务),使M1在2020年急剧增加,导致速度暴跌。(信贷:圣美联储银行)路易,你好吗?

c9.original: In a neoclassical view, monetary policy affects only the price level, not the level of output in the economy. For example, an expansionary monetary policy causes aggregate demand to shift from the original AD0 to AD1. However, the adjustment of the economy from the original equilibrium (E0) to the new equilibrium (E1) represents an inflationary increase in the price level from P0 to P1, but has no effect in the long run on output or the unemployment rate. In fact, no shift in AD will affect the equilibrium quantity of output in this model.
c9.zh: 在新古典主义观点中,货币政策只影响价格水平,而不是经济中的产出水平. 例如,扩张性的货币政策导致总需求从最初的AD0转向AD1。 然而,经济从最初的平衡(E0)调整到新的平衡(E1)意味着价格水平从P0上升至P1,但从长远来看对产出或失业率没有影响。 事实上,反倾销的任何变化都不会影响这一模型中产出的均衡数量。
